tools.name: verify_email
tools.description: Verify a single email address using Webbula's 20+ year email-intelligence dataset. Returns a deliverability verdict, any corrected form, and a trust block (data provenance and activity history) so an agent can decide whether the address is safe to use. Real-time, single tool call.

profile.description: Optional Webbula hygiene profile name. Defaults to the server's configured profile.

tools.name: hygiene_check
tools.description: Run Webbula's full email hygiene analysis on one or more addresses. For each email you get its classification, activity history (first/last seen, trajectory), a corrected form when a typo is detected, and a trust block. Use this when you need the full picture — threats, spam-trap/complainer risk, and provenance — not just a yes/no. Accepts 1..100 addresses per call.

emails.description: The email addresses to check (1..100). Larger lists belong in the batch flow.

profile.description: Optional Webbula hygiene profile name. Defaults to the server's configured profile.

tools.name: get_credits
tools.description: Check the Webbula account's remaining credit balance before running a larger job. Returns remaining credits per billing scenario, with an explicit "unlimited" flag for accounts that are not metered. Does not consume verification credits.

tools.name: list_profiles
tools.description: List the Webbula profiles your account is allowed to use. A profile (or preset) selects the verification/hygiene/lead validations and the billing scenario a call runs under. Use this to discover valid profile names before calling verify_email, hygiene_check, validate_lead, or upload_file — those tools reject a profile that is not on this list.

tools.name: validate_lead
tools.description: Validate a full lead/contact record with Webbula's leadHygiene. Parses and assesses any combination of name, postal address, and phone number — modeled gender, address accuracy and geocode, phone line type — and, when an email is supplied, runs the same email hygiene verdict as verify_email in the same call. Use this for cleaning CRM/lead records, not just an email address. At least one of first_name, last_name, full_address, phone, or emails is required. Real-time, single tool call.

profile.description: Optional lead-enabled Webbula profile name. Defaults to the server's configured lead profile.

full_address.description: The complete address: street, city, state, and ZIP.

emails.description: Optional email addresses to additionally run hygiene on (max 100).

tools.name: upload_file
tools.description: Submit a file of emails for asynchronous batch hygiene when the list is too large for the real-time tools. Provide the file inline (base64 + filename) or point at a remote source (web URL, FTP, or SSH). Returns a package_name to track with file_status and fetch with download_results. Accepts .csv, .txt, .xlsx, .xls. Local filesystem paths are not supported.

profile.description: Optional Webbula profile name. Defaults to the server's configured profile.

content_base64.description: Base64-encoded file content (≤ ~1 MiB). Use with `filename`.

filename.description: File name (with a .csv/.txt/.xlsx/.xls extension). Required with `content_base64`.

data_source.description: Remote source type, as an alternative to inline content.

secure.description: Use TLS (SFTP) for the FTP source.

tools.name: file_status
tools.description: Check the status of a batch task by its package_name. Returns the current stage (preparing → prepared → running → finished → completed, or canceled) with a human-readable label and whether it is terminal, plus — once completed — the list of result files ready to download. Poll this after upload_file until the task is terminal.

package_name.description: The task handle returned by upload_file.

tools.name: download_results
tools.description: Download a result file from a completed batch task. Provide the package_name and a filename reported by file_status (e.g. insert.csv for cleaned records, _report.xls for the summary). Returns the file content unchanged — text files as text, binary files base64-encoded.

filename.description: A result filename reported by file_status (e.g. insert.csv, _report.xls).
